baseline._about: What the learner already knows: a Kotlin developer who has built an Android app (Gradle, coroutines, Flow), and has heard iOS apps are written in Swift.

compiler.def: The program that turns source code into something a machine can run.

front end.def: The part of the compiler that reads and checks your code, the same for every target.

back end.def: The part of the compiler that produces output for one kind of machine.

target.def: A platform Kotlin can compile for: the JVM, Android, iOS, the web, desktop.

bytecode.def: Encoded instructions read by a program such as the JVM or ART.

native code.def: Machine code that runs directly on the CPU, with no virtual machine.

w0.def: An Arm register in the addition example.

w1.def: A second Arm register in the addition example.

add w1, w0, w1.def: Arm addition with w1 as the destination.

Kotlin/Native.def: Kotlin's back end that produces native code, built on LLVM.

source set.def: A folder of code compiled for a chosen set of targets.

commonMain.def: The source set compiled for every target.

androidMain.def: The source set compiled only for Android.

iosMain.def: The source set compiled only for iOS.

common code.def: Code in commonMain: shared by every target.

expect.def: A declaration in common code that promises each platform will provide it.

actual.def: A platform's implementation of an expect declaration.

framework.def: Apple's package for a library: the compiled code plus a description of its API.

Objective-C.def: The older language of Apple's platforms, which Swift can call directly.

header.def: The file that describes a library's API, without its code.

completion handler.def: A function you pass in, called later with the result: Objective-C's way of saying "later".

@Throws.def: Lists which Kotlin exceptions may cross into Swift as errors.

shared heap.def: Kotlin/Native's one pool of objects, reachable from any thread.

tracing GC.def: A garbage collector that starts from the roots, follows every reference, and frees what it didn't reach.

main queue.def: The line of tasks waiting for iOS's main thread: the MessageQueue's role.

cancellation.def: Stopping a coroutine or task before it finishes.

umbrella framework.def: One framework that carries every Kotlin module Swift needs, with one runtime.

dead code elimination.def: Leaving out compiled code nothing uses, to keep the app small.

Compose Multiplatform.def: JetBrains' version of Jetpack Compose that runs on Android, iOS, desktop and web.

Compose runtime.def: The part of Compose that tracks state and decides what to recompose; it knows nothing about pixels.

platform layer.def: The part written per target: the window, touches, the drawing surface, text input and accessibility.

Skia.def: A graphics library that draws shapes and text; on iOS, Compose draws with it through Skiko.

ComposeUIViewController.def: Hosts Compose UI inside an iOS app as one UIKit view controller.

accessibility tree.def: The list of on-screen elements, with labels and roles, that VoiceOver reads.

UIKitView.def: Places a real UIKit view, such as a map, inside a Compose screen.

platform library.def: A prebuilt Kotlin binding to a target's native libraries, shipped with Kotlin/Native; on Apple targets, to Apple's frameworks.

UIKit.def: Apple's framework for screens: buttons, lists, text.

Swift.def: The language of iOS apps, close to Kotlin.

Xcode.def: Apple's IDE: builds and runs iOS apps, like Android Studio.

view controller.def: Manages one iOS screen's views and reacts to the user, like an Activity.

SwiftUI.def: Apple's declarative UI framework, the iOS counterpart of Compose.

heap.def: The memory area where objects are created and kept.

root.def: A reference the program certainly still has, like a local or global variable; tracing starts from the roots.

reference counting.def: Freeing each object the moment its count of strong references reaches zero; Swift calls it ARC.

strong reference.def: A reference that keeps its object alive by adding to its count.

cycle.def: Objects that hold each other with strong references, so none of their counts reaches zero.

deinit.def: Code in a Swift class that runs when an instance is freed.

weak reference.def: A reference that doesn't add to the count, so it can't keep its object alive; it becomes nil when the object is freed.

closure.def: Swift's lambda: a block of code that holds strong references to what it uses.

[weak self].def: A capture list that makes a closure hold self weakly.

run loop.def: iOS's version of the Looper: keeps the main thread waiting for work and handling it.

composable.def: A Kotlin function marked @Composable that describes UI for its data.

recomposition.def: Compose calling composables again because their data changed.

state.def: Data whose change makes Compose recompose what uses it.

Compose compiler plugin.def: Part of the Kotlin compiler that rewrites composables so the runtime can track what each one showed.

JVM.def: The Java Virtual Machine: a program that runs compiled Kotlin and Java on any computer.

async function.def: Swift's version of a suspend function, called with await.

Task.def: Swift's version of a launched coroutine.

scope.def: A CoroutineScope: the owner of a group of coroutines; cancelling it cancels them all.

XCFramework.def: One bundle holding framework or library variants for selected Apple platforms and architectures.

semantics.def: What each UI element is and says (role, label), which Compose passes to accessibility tools.

multiplatform plugin.def: The Gradle plugin, kotlin("multiplatform"), that reads the kotlin { } block and sets up targets, source sets and compilations.

kotlin { }.def: The block in a shared module's build.gradle.kts that declares its targets and source sets.

iosArm64.def: The iOS target for real iPhones.

iosSimulatorArm64.def: The iOS target for the simulator on an Apple-silicon Mac.

platform source set.def: The source set made for exactly one target and named after it, such as androidMain or iosArm64Main.

iosArm64Main.def: The platform source set of the iosArm64 target.

compilation.def: One compiler run for one target, over every source set that target uses: main for your code, test for your tests.

commonTest.def: The test source set compiled for every target, beside commonMain.

intermediate source set.def: A source set compiled for some, but not all, of the project's targets, such as iosMain.

default hierarchy template.def: The multiplatform plugin's built-in tree of intermediate source sets; it creates the ones that fit the targets you declare.

appleMain.def: The intermediate source set compiled for every Apple target in the project.

nativeMain.def: The intermediate source set compiled for every Kotlin/Native target in the project.

dependsOn.def: The link from a source set to the one above it: it sees that one's code, can keep its expect promises, and gets its libraries.

multiplatform library.def: A library published for many targets with one common API, so commonMain can use it.

commonMain.dependencies.def: The dependencies block of one source set; iosMain.dependencies and the others work the same way.

androidLibrary.def: The older name of the Android target block, before version 8.12 of Android's plugin.

iosX64.def: The iOS target for the simulator on a Mac with an Intel chip.

klib.def: A Kotlin/Native library file: a zip, for one target, holding the code as IR, a description of its declarations and a manifest.

IR.def: Intermediate representation: the compiler's own checked form of the code, after the front end and before any machine code.

publication.def: A separately named package of a library's files in a repository; a multiplatform library has one per target plus a root.

Gradle module metadata.def: A file format published next to a library (the .module file) that lists the library's variants for Gradle.

variant.def: One version of a library, built for one kind of consumer and tagged with attributes such as its target.

dependency injection.def: Handing an object what it depends on from outside, instead of letting it create it.

dependency injection framework.def: A library, such as Koin, that builds objects and hands each one what it needs, from rules you write.

ios_arm64.def: How Kotlin/Native writes the iosArm64 target's name inside a klib and in published metadata.

ios_simulator_arm64.def: How Kotlin/Native writes the iosSimulatorArm64 target's name in published metadata.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what. The lint fails on them (any page text, labels, questions); say the named actor or the plain word instead.

phrases.the system: name the actor: system_server, the kernel, or Binder
phrases.views: say buttons and text, or the screen (View isn't taught)
phrases.lost focus: say: another app is in front
phrases.simply: cut it: it makes a learner who's stuck feel slow
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is
